impact: Shipped in 0.1.0 by recorded owner-authorized decision (2026-08-02, option 2): the README 'Known wording bug' note (README.md:97) documents the contradiction, so the user-facing harm is a misleading remedy in an error reachable only under a misconfigured CCUSAGE_CMD. Remaining scope is the 0.1.1 clean fix only: reword src/ccusage.ts:36's frozen-oracle text, add the numbered ALLOWLIST entry and comparison-policy update, and cover the deliberate divergence from usage.py:117 in the parity harness, through a reviewed cycle. Nothing gates on it.
resolution: Resolved 2026-08-02 in commit 51e0a42, the way the issue always wanted: the ENOENT diagnostic now says 'Fix or unset CCUSAGE_CMD — spendbar bundles its own ccusage and has no npx fallback' instead of parroting usage.py's install-npx advice. Sanctioned as ALLOWLIST-25 via a stderr REWRITE comparison policy (mirror of help-config-path): only the advice suffix is rewritten in the oracle's output, everything else — the quoted command, single stderr line, empty stdout, exit 1 — stays byte-compared. A first-draft pattern policy was rejected in codex review for accepting any executable name; the review's regression scenario is now a dedicated test. Mutation-verified (wording revert 273/1, policy deletion, scope-line deletion all fail loudly). Ships in 0.1.1 (publish awaits fresh owner authorization).
title: Frozen ENOENT diagnostic advises installing npx, which is never the remedy — reword in 0.1.1 (rescoped, shipped as-is in 0.1.0)
